newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Moves to approve EU patent law provoke alarm.
newsitem.headline: Moves to approve EU patent law provoke alarm.

text.p: Members of the European Parliament reacted in outrage on Thursday to moves to approve a draft EU law allowing multinational food and drugs firms to patent parts of humans, animals and plants.
"It gives (biotechnology companies) a monopoly on genes and on food resources," German Green Euro-MP Hildrud Breyer told Reuters.

The draft EU directive, which aims to harmonise member states' national patent laws, was approved by the parliament's legal affairs committee on Wednesday night and will be put to the full parliament in July.

The draft law rules out human cloning -- the creation of a new person from the single cell of another -- but it permits patents on plants and elements of humans and animals, including their genes, if these elements have been isolated from the body.

The European Alliance of Genetic Support Groups praised the legal committee's move, saying that letting companies "own" the building blocks of life would encourage them to invest in research into incurable gene-diseases like cancer or epilepsy.

German Socialist Willi Rothley, who persuaded the legal affairs committee to support the draft law, said the proposal was much better than an earlier bill on biotechnological inventions drafted by the Commission in 1988 and thrown out by Euro-MPs in 1995.
But critical Euro-MPs said the law would hinder research.
"If I own the DNA (gene code) you won't be able to develop an application for it unless you buy the licence from me," Breyer said.

Greek Christian Democrat Euro-MP Antonios Trakatellis, a biochemistry professor, said it was right to reward innovation by awarding patents to processes which used or changed genes to create a different product, such as using the insulin gene to develop a process for manufacturing insulin outside the body.

But he said it was wrong to give a commercial company a monopoly over a newly discovered gene, especially when scientists already possessed the means to discover every human gene between now and the year 2010.
Other scientists in the EU assembly shared his concerns, Trakatellis said.
A leading Indian scientist told a news conference in Brussels on Wednesday that the EU's draft patent law would allow multinational companies to plunder the developing world.

"This is giving licence to take the last resource that allows people to survive in the third world, which is their biodiversity and their knowledge of how to use it for nutrition," Vandana Shiva of India's Research Foundation for Science, Technology and Natural Resource Policy said.
